newsitem.title: INDIA: India to test fire short-range missiles - agency.
newsitem.headline: India to test fire short-range missiles - agency.

text.p: India will test fire an indigenously developed short range anti-aircraft missile at its Chandipur test range in the eastern state of Orissa next week, the United News of India (UNI) said on Thursday.
The test fire has been tentatively fixed for some time between December 16 and December 23, UNI said, quoting unnamed official sources.

In preparation for the test, two Trishul missiles have been moved to the test range from the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) at Hyderabad in southern Andhra Pradesh state, it said.
India has had little success with its short-range anti-aircraft missile programme, even though it has so far test fired about 30 Trishul missiles, UNI said.
In the latest test, the Trishul missiles will be fired from a mobile launcher at Chandipur-on-Sea, 14 kilometres (nine miles) from Balasore, in Orissa.
The Trishul, named for the trident carried by the Hindu god Shiva, has a range of 500 metres to nine kilometres (five miles), and can carry a 15-kilogram warhead.
The weapon is part of India's integrated weapons programme which includes surface-to-surface, surface-to-air and anti-tank missiles. The Trishul can be used by the army, navy or air force.

Last week, India bowed to western pressure and rolled back its nuclear programme when it decided to shelve the deployment of Agni, its intermediate-range ballistic missile capable of carrying nuclear warheads, after successfully completing research on the missile.
The Agni is designed to hit targets 2,500 kilometres (1,500 miles) away.

The United States, fearing an arms race between India and pakistan, has urged New Delhi to halt missile testing permanently. The South Asian neighbours have fought three wars since independence from Britain in 1947.
India detonated a nuclear device in 1974 but says it has not built a nuclear bomb. The United States believes both India and Pakistan could quickly assemble nuclear weapons.
